 Skin Care 
 We tested La Roche-Posay’s bestselling anti-aging products. These worked best for our skin concerns
 By Michelle Rae Uy , CNN Underscored
 Published
 8:00 AM EST, Thu November 19, 2026
 Link Copied!
 Michelle Rae Uy/CNN Underscored 
 In this article 
 Cleansers 
 Serums 
 Moisturizers 
 Sunscreens 
 Body care 
 Bottom line 
 FAQs 
 Meet our panel 
 Meet our experts 
 Why trust CNN Underscored 
 La Roche-Posay is one of the world’s most recognizable skin care brands. Many would argue, myself included, that it’s also one of the best. It “combines science with clinically supported ingredients,” according to Dr. Sejal K. Shah , a board-certified dermatologist and founder of SmarterSkin Dermatology , “The formulations are very thoughtful. The pricing is accessible. [And] they are trying to make products that are tolerable for most individuals.”
 The L’Oréal-owned brand doesn’t just make bestselling acne treatments, face moisturizers and face sunscreens . It’s also known for its anti-aging products , which support the skin at any phase of life, helping smooth lines and fight damage.
 I’ve been a fan of La Roche-Posay for years and use several of its products regularly, including the Effaclar Multi-Target Acne Treatment with Salicylic Acid for breakouts and the iconic Thermal Spring Water Face Mist . But now that I’m feeling the side effects of having mature skin , including loss of elasticity and dryness, I wanted to see which of its anti-aging products are worth adding to my routine. I enlisted the help of colleagues in their 20s, 30s and 40s to find out.
 Cleansers
 La Roche-Posay Toleriane Purifying Foaming Face Wash 
 La Roche-Posay 
 A gentle cleanser that not only removes impurities but also helps support your skin barrier, this is a great product for those with sensitive skin.
 From $9 at La Roche-Posay
 $16 
 From $12 at Amazon
 From $18 at Ulta Beauty
 Many dermatologists recommend La Roche-Posay cleansers for sensitive skin , but some users say they’re too gentle to do the job. I had four testers from our panel test two of the brand’s cleansers — the Toleriane Hydrating Gentle Facial Cleanser and the Toleriane Purifying Foaming Face Wash — and three said the cleansers struggled to remove makeup on the first wash. Overall, the foaming formula had more favorable feedback, though the Hydrating Gentle Facial Cleanser is still a good option for those with sensitive skin.
 Both CNN Underscored social coordinator Gabriella Triolo and editorial coordinator Stephanie Luna said the foaming cleanser does a great job cleansing their faces and leaving them clean and refreshed without feeling tight or too dry. Both appreciate its gentle formulation, with Triolo saying that it doesn’t make her break out, which is a huge plus for her. And Luna said that even though it struggles a little to remove eye makeup, it removes the rest without requiring a second wash.
 Gabriella Triolo/CNN Underscored 
 After a month of use, neither has experienced any anti-aging effects. However, it’s also good to note that La Roche-Posay only advertises it as a product that helps maintain your skin’s “natural moisture barrier and pH” so it’s really more for removing impurities and supporting your skin, which is just as important for anti-aging.
 Triolo isn’t a fan of the tube’s dispenser, calling it “the worst packaging” she’s ever used because it dispenses the product too fast and “gets [it] all over everything.” Luna pointed out that it might be better dispensed via a pump, and the 400-milliliter bottle, which you can also buy refills for, does come with one. If you love this cleanser, that might be the best option.
 Molly Flores/CNN Underscored 
 Related article 
 10 drugstore face washes that actually work, according to dermatologists 
 What we liked about it: Its formulation is gentle and effectively removes impurities, leaving your skin refreshed and hydrated.
 What we didn’t like about it: The tube packaging dispenses the product too fast. The product doesn’t foam as much as expected.
 Serums
 La Roche-Posay Hyalu B5 Pure Hyaluronic Acid Serum 
 La Roche-Posay Hyalu B5 Serum 
 Amazon 
 This anti-aging serum is highly effective, delivering fast hydration and managing fine lines. However, the added fragrance is not great news for those with sensitive skin.
 From $40 at Amazon
 From $40 at Walmart
 From $40 at La Roche-Posay
 From $43 at Ulta Beauty
 Applying hyaluronic acid to dry skin can make it feel sticky or tacky, which is why our associate testing writer Maxwell Shukuya and Luna thought the Hyalu B5 Pure Hyaluronic Acid Serum felt “a little slimy,” as Shukuya described it, at first. The good news is that Shukuya discovered that he just needs to give his skin a minute or two to completely absorb the serum, and Luna realized, after a couple of uses, that “the formula works better on slightly damp skin.”
 After overcoming that initial hurdle, both testers now love this product, thanks to its anti-aging benefits. They praise its lightweight, non-greasy texture that absorbs well into the skin and its near-instant results. They love how hydrated and plump it makes their skin feel, with Luna noticing improvements in her fine lines, particularly around the mouth and nose. “They’re still there, but they seem a little less pronounced after a month,” she said.
 Maxwell Shukuya/CNN Underscored 
 Both appreciate the dropper the Hyalu B5 Pure Hyaluronic Acid Serum comes with, as it makes application convenient, even for someone like Shukuya who’s never used a face serum until now. And, according to Luna, it’s a great fit for her routine, especially on days she didn’t want to apply a heavy moisturizer. “This is a quick product to apply and [less messy] than a cream or lotion,” she said.
 It does have a floral fragrance, though both testers agreed it is subtle enough that they don’t mind it. Luna thinks that it actually gives it a refreshing, clean scent. That may still be a downside for those with sensitive skin, though, since the product page lists parfum or fragrance in the ingredients. La Roche-Posay says it’s an allergy-tested formula, but it might be a good idea to do a patch test at home to be on the safe side.
 Maxwell Shukuya/CNN Underscored 
 What we liked about it: Its anti-aging formula works well for rehydrating skin, improving elasticity and minimizing fine lines.
 What we didn’t like about it: The added fragrance might not make it ideal for sensitive skin.
 La Roche-Posay Vitamin C12 Serum 
 Amazon 
 This vitamin C serum was one of the most effective products we tested, but it was also the most divisive. However, while some don't mind its side effects, others do.
 $45 
 From $36 at Amazon
 $45 at Walmart
 $45 at La Roche-Posay
 $47 at Ulta Beauty
 It’s a little harder to champion this serum. On one hand, the La Roche-Posay Vitamin C12 Serum has proven very effective. CNN Underscored photo editor Molly Flores and managing editor Rachel Quigley said it helps their faces look brighter and feel plumper. Flores even noted that it healed some of her post-breakout spots. Neither loved its thick consistency, but on the upside, they both said it sinks into the skin quickly, with Flores going so far as to say that it’s one of the best-absorbing serums she’s ever used.
 It has some ride-or-die fans too, including Triolo, who wasn’t technically one of its testers for this story but has been using it daily as part of her skin care routine. She’s such a big fan that she wanted to weigh in and say it has made a huge improvement to her acne-scarred skin .
 Rachel Quigley/CNN Underscored 
 However, it also comes with two very noticeable side effects. As with many vitamin C serums, it leaves a temporary yellowish tinge on the skin, which Quigley isn’t a fan of. Worse, it has a noticeable smell that she said lasts about 30 minutes. Although neither of these bothered Flores and Triolo enough to influence their opinions, Quigley couldn’t wait to go back to her regular serum.
 Whether you should add the Vitamin C12 Serum is up to you. According to Dr. Brianna Olamiju , a board-certified dermatologist at Spring Street Dermatology , “Incorporating an antioxidant like vitamin C can be important, especially in high-pollution areas where there are free radicals in the air that can cause skin damage,” she said. But with this formula in particular, it may be worth weighing its brightening and anti-aging benefits against its side effects, especially since it isn’t exactly cheap and there are many excellent vitamin C alternatives on the market.
 What we liked about it: It supports your skin barrier, is fast-absorbing and is very good at brightening and hydration.
 What we didn’t like about it: It has a noticeable smell and leaves an orange or yellow tinge.
 Molly Flores/CNN Underscored 
 Related article 
 The best anti-aging products to tackle wrinkles and lines, according to dermatologists 
 La Roche-Posay Anthelios AOX Antioxidant Serum with SPF 50 Sunscreen 
 Amazon 
 This two-in-one product helps with skin hydration and protection against UV rays so you can whittle down your morning skin care routine.
 $45 at Amazon
 $45 at Walmart
 $45 at La Roche-Posay
 The Anthelios AOX Antioxidant Serum with SPF 50 is another highly rated product from La Roche-Posay, and both testers on our panel agree it’s well worth the money. CNN Underscored outdoors and sustainable living editor Kai Burkhardt said that the high SPF rating gives him confidence and our digital content strategist Madison Yerke said it’s been great for the unseasonably warm weather in New York this fall.
 Madison Yerke/CNN Underscored 
 As a long-distance runner who trains every day and applies sunscreen twice in the morning — once before her morning run and again after her post-run shower — Yerke appreciates its easy application and staying power. “It takes only one or two passes to rub in, which makes it easy to grab and apply when I’m running late or in a hurry before rushing out the door,” she said. “This sunscreen also doesn’t come off while or after a run — a huge win.”
 As an anti-aging serum, it’s not particularly groundbreaking. Neither tester noticed any improvement in their fine lines and dark spots, and Burkhardt tested it for a month. However, Burkhardt feels that it’s a nourishing formula, leaving his skin softer, and Yerke said that it makes her skin glossy and glowy, albeit slightly greasy, which she doesn’t mind because it still feels like she’s not wearing sunscreen. Both testers also love the fragrance-free formula’s texture and consistency, saying it’s lightweight and absorbs quickly.
 Kai Burkhardt/CNN Underscored 
 If you’re looking for a preventative anti-aging product, this serum with SPF is a great option that promotes hydration and protects against UV rays. However, if you’re looking for something to reverse signs of aging, you might want to look elsewhere.
 What we liked about it: You get two products in one: a hydrating serum and an effective sunscreen, which can help pare down your morning routine. It’s great for busy individuals.
 What we didn’t like about it: It doesn’t exactly deliver on its promise to “visibly improve the appearance of fine lines [and] dark spots.” Burkhardt also said that the nozzle tends to leak.
 La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Dark Spot Serum With Melasyl + Niacinamide 
 Amazon 
 Taking a gentler approach to reducing discoloration, this serum boasts La Roche-Posay’s latest hero ingredient, Melasyl.
 From $45 at Amazon
 $45 at Ulta Beauty
 From $45 at La Roche-Posay
 If you’re not familiar with Melasyl, it’s La Roche-Posay’s multi-patented, sensitive skin-friendly ingredient that launched in early 2024 and is designed as a dark spot corrector . And it’s one of the active ingredients in the Mela B3 Dark Spot Serum, which CNN Underscored beauty and fashion editor Sophie Shaw is calling “a good alternative to harsher active ingredients that are typically used for discoloration.”
 The question is, does the ingredient work? It does in the Mela B3 Dual Body Discoloration Treatment, which I also reviewed below, and very well too — unsurprisingly, since the brand dedicated 18 years of research to it. However, it’s a gradual change that requires consistent use, which is probably why Shaw and Triolo didn’t notice any difference after two weeks of using this serum version. It’s also worth bearing in mind that neither had hyperpigmentation on their faces before they started using the serum so the change may not be obvious.
 Gabriella Triolo/CNN Underscored 
 Triolo said that it’s too sticky for her, but that may just be due to the niacinamide — applying too much of it on the skin leads to that tacky feeling. Shaw, on the other hand, said that the serum is light, not sticky and sinks into her skin quickly.
 I wouldn’t say it’s as divisive as the vitamin C serum, but Triolo does not like the added fragrance, and you might not either if you have sensitive skin. Meanwhile, Shaw thinks that the scent is pleasant.
 What we liked about it: It’s a gentle treatment for dark spots that can be used in tandem with other brightening products, like exfoliating serums or toners , but it won’t cause the dryness or peeling that can come with chemical exfoliants.
 What we didn’t like about it: The formula is stickier than the other serums we tested and some may want to avoid the fragranced formula.
 Moisturizers
 Best Tested 
 La Roche-Posay Cicaplast Balm B5+ Soothing Therapeutic Multi-Purpose Cream 
 Amazon 
 Very effective at treating dry, cracked and irritated skin, this La Roche-Posay cream isn’t just great for anti-aging. It’s also good for eczema , dry winter skin and more.
 Read our review 
 $19 
 From $14 at Amazon
 From $19 at Walmart
 From $19 at La Roche-Posay
 From $21 at Ulta Beauty
 Testers Yerke and Luna have different opinions about the Cicaplast Balm B5+ Soothing Therapeutic Multi-Purpose Cream’s consistency. Although Yerke thinks it has a “medium creamy texture that’s fairly lightweight,” she also finds it a little challenging to apply and feels that if she doesn’t rub it in extensively, it just sits on top of her skin.
 On the other hand, Luna finds the texture thick and heavy. However, she said it also absorbs quickly, doesn’t feel greasy and doesn’t rub off easily. “Usually creams tend to feel so thick that I’m worried they’ll get on my bedsheets,” she said, “But this one [wasn’t like that] at all.”
 Stephanie Luna/CNN Underscored 
 They might not agree on the texture, but both are on the same page about how effective this balm is — which aligns with the other testing we’ve done pitting it against other top-rated moisturizers for dry skin . La Roche-Posay advertises it as a “therapeutic balm to soothe dry, cracked and irritated skin,” and as such, it’s proven to be very effective. Luna, who uses it on her hands, elbows, feet and arms, as well as on her eczema flare-ups, said that it has done “a great job at hydrating from the first use” and continues to deliver noticeable gradual improvements to even the worst eczema spots where her skin starts to crack. Yerke also added that the moisturizing effect is immediate: “After being rubbed in, I could see a difference right away.”
 Both also agree that the packaging makes dispensing effortless, although Yerke said that the time-consuming application makes her hesitate adding it to her morning routine. As for the price point, Luna thinks it’s a little expensive for how much of the product you’re getting. However, the Cicaplast Balm B5+ Soothing Therapeutic Multi-Purpose Cream’s performance, combined with its gentle formula that makes it ideal for babies and adults with sensitive skin, means it’ll go a long way. As someone who suffers from dry hands, I might get this one for myself too.
 If you favor a lightweight moisturizer, you may consider the La Roche-Posay Hyalu B5 Suractivated Hyaluronic Acid Anti-Aging Face Cream , which we also tested. While it didn’t wow the testers overall when it came to anti-aging benefits, it was a nice gel-cream hydrator.
 What we liked about it: It’s proven to be very effective at what it was developed for, delivering fast results and incremental improvements to problem areas. It remains our best-tested pick for moisturizing dry skin.
 What we didn’t like about it: Some users might find it time-consuming to apply.
 La Roche-Posay Toleriane Double Repair Moisturizing Drops 
 La Roche-Posay 
 An easy addition and affordable addition to your skin care routine, these hydrating drops is effective at restoring and supporting your skin barrier.
 $20 at Ulta Beauty
 $20 at Walmart
 $20 at La Roche-Posay
 Michelle Rae Uy/CNN Underscored 
 Olamiju is a huge advocate for supporting the skin barrier, especially as your skin matures and if you’re using highly drying active ingredients such as retinoids . This surprisingly affordable serum-slash-moisturizer from La Roche-Posay is a great way to do just that, developed to support the skin barrier, provide hydration and deliver near-immediate, long-lasting effects.
 Triolo might need a little more convincing on its long-term benefits, as she feels like it hasn’t really been seeping into her skin deep enough to make a difference. However, she does think “it’s super hydrating.” As does Shaw, who also finds that it sinks into her skin quickly and makes it plumper.
 Sophie Shaw/CNN Underscored 
 Both appreciate its lightweight, non-greasy, fragrance-free formula and the easy-dispensing squeeze bottle, which makes it effortless to add to their daytime routines. And both love the idea of using it with other hydrating products. Shaw already layers it over the Mela B3 Dark Spot Serum With Melasyl + Niacinamide on the driest areas of her face and at night under her nighttime retinol, which is its perfect use. Triolo, on the other hand, is planning to pair it “with a more intense moisturizer” during the winter months.
 If your skin needs a little more support, whether you’re suffering from dry skin or a compromised skin barrier, this is a low-effort, low-cost addition to your anti-aging regimen.
 What we liked about it: It’s cheap, effective at supporting your skin barrier and an easy addition to your routine.
 What we didn’t like about it: Its long-term effects are still in question.
 Sunscreens
 La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVAir SPF 50 Mineral Serum Sunscreen 
 La Roche-Posay 
 Surprisingly lightweight, this broad-spectrum mineral sunscreen effectively blocks UVA and UVB rays and leaves very minimal white cast due to the brand’s Miner-All technology.
 $43 
 $38 at Amazon
 $43 at Ulta Beauty
 $43 at La Roche-Posay
 Mineral sunscreens contain zinc or titanium oxide, which Olamiju said block out the sun’s UV rays physically. Those ingredients tend to leave a white cast, which makes mineral sunscreens less ideal for people with darker skin.
 La Roche-Posay seems to have solved the white-cast dilemma with the Anthelios UVAir SPF 50 Mineral Serum Sunscreen. Thanks to what the brand calls its MINER-ALL technology, it leaves a minimal white cast on my skin — so minimal, in fact, that I hardly see it right after application, and it’s not noticeable at all when I’m sweating. As someone who’s gone on runs and hikes feeling confident, only to discover halfway through that my sweat looks milky white from my sunscreen, I’ve become a huge fan.
 Of course, its UV-blocking performance is impressive as well. Triolo said that it might be the best sunscreen she’s ever used. It feels effective against both UVA and UVB rays in our daily use, and the formula is lightweight and easy to blend. I do feel like the formula is ever so slightly greasy, but because it’s, as Triolo puts it, “so thin that it feels like you have nothing on,” this isn’t a deal-breaker, especially if you’re a mineral sunscreen fan who hates the white cast side-effect.
 Michelle Rae Uy/CNN Underscored 
 Sunscreens don’t traditionally protect your skin from free radicals in the air, but La Roche-Posay claims that this one does, thanks to the antioxidants in its formula. That’s a welcome added anti-aging benefit, especially for folks living in big cities, as studies show that air pollution contributes to cell aging and inflammation.
 We also both love the bottle it comes in. It’s portable, so it’s small bag-friendly, and has a thin nozzle at the top that makes dispensing easy, especially if you use the two-finger application method . Adding this to your daily routine, even on a busy schedule, should be effortless.
 Overall, the Anthelios UVAir SPF 50 Mineral Serum Sunscreen has converted both of us. It turned me into a mineral sunscreen fan, and Triolo said it’s so good she switched from her old sunscreen.
 What we liked about it: It’s highly effective as sun protection, barely leaves a white cast and is effortless to apply. La Roche-Posay also claims that it’s “supercharged with antioxidants” to help minimize the effects of air pollution.
 What we didn’t like about it: It has a slightly greasy finish, which might be a problem if you live in a very humid area.
 La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVAir SPF 50 Serum Sunscreen 
 La Roche-Posay 
 To round out your anti-aging regiment, this chemical sunscreen boasts an invisible finish, a lightweight formula and effective UV blocking.
 $40 
 $32 at Amazon
 $40 at Walmart
 $40 at Ulta Beauty
 $40 at La Roche-Posay
 If you’re looking for sunscreen with a matte finish, the La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVAir SPF 50 Serum Sunscreen might not be for you. That’s what Shukuya realized during testing. He stopped using it after two weeks because the formula felt too greasy for his taste and made his skin look “shiny,” which he didn’t like. But that’s just personal preference.
 Shukuya said he appreciates the product’s “skin care-forward ingredients on top of chemical sun blockers” and its effectiveness against harmful UV rays. Flores and Luna agree, with Flores saying her skin “felt protected against pollution,” supporting the brand’s claim that it’s “supercharged with antioxidants.”
 Stephanie Luna/CNN Underscored 
 The Anthelios UVAir SPF 50 Serum Sunscreen may not have the matte effect Shukuya prefers, but it has a lightweight, zero-white-cast finish that the other two testers loved. Neither thought the formula was greasy. Flores said it absorbs quickly and feels amazing on her skin. Meanwhile, Luna appreciates that it blends out well, gives her a dewy, glowy look and has an invisible finish, which is unsurprising since chemical sunscreens are designed to absorb quickly and don’t have the ingredients that leave a white cast.
 All three testers agree that the packaging is excellent. Just like the mineral version, it’s compact, portable and “easy to control without making a mess,” according to Luna.
 Get its mineral counterpart if you like the idea of physical UV block. But the Anthelios UVAir SPF 50 Serum Sunscreen is the better choice if you’re comfortable with chemical sunscreen filters and don’t want to worry about white streaks on your skin.
 What we liked about it: Its invisible finish, easy-to-use packaging and lightweight formula that’s highly effective at blocking UV rays make it a great chemical sunscreen option for anti-aging protection.
 What we didn’t like about it: If you want a matte finish, this isn’t for you.
 La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense SPF 50 Sunscreen 
 Amazon 
 This sunscreen is La Roche Posay's lightest and most comfortable sunscreen yet, thanks to a new chemical sunscreen filter.
 $40 at Amazon
 $40 at Ulta Beauty
 $40 at La Roche-Posay
 Earlier this year, the US Food and Drug Administration approved the first new sunscreen filter in 20 years. Bemotrizinol, or BEMT, is a chemical UV filter that comes with more robust UVA and UVB protection and more promising safety data. It also lends itself to lighter-feeling formulas that are easier to blend and white cast-free. That’s certainly the case for the Anthelios UVDefense sunscreen, which has a serum-like texture that spreads over the skin effortlessly.
 Michelle Rae Uy/CNN Underscored 
 Similar to the Anthelios UVAir serum sunscreen, this formula leaves the skin with a glowy, perhaps slightly greasy finish. Shaw said it adds a bit of shine to her skin immediately after application, but it seems to look more balanced after it dries down for a couple minutes. She noted that it’s a good option for layering as it doesn’t pill on top of her moisturizer or under her foundation. It also has added antioxidant protection built in with La Roche-Posay’s Cell-OX Shield Technology to protect from environmental stressors and pollution. Shaw, who has tested dozens of sunscreens, said it’s one of the best options she’s tried for a truly serum-like application experience.
 What we liked about it: This sunscreen serum has a weightless feel and invisible finish.
 What we didn’t like about it: It leaves skin shinier than before.
 Body care
 La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Dual-Body Discoloration Treatment 
 Amazon 
 This light and effective body lotion works well at skin smoothing and brightening. It’s an anti-aging must.
 $28 at Amazon
 $28 at Amazon
 $28 at Ulta Beauty
 $28 at La Roche-Posay
 Our panel testers didn’t test this groundbreaking product from La Roche-Posay, but our CNN Underscored Innovation Awards beauty team, which I am a part of, did, and we love it. It’s the first body treatment with Melasyl as its main active ingredient.
 All five people on the beauty team praised the lotion’s effective formula that sinks into your skin quickly and delivers near-immediate smoothing results. CNN Underscored money writer Robin Rothstein gives it props for “improving the smoothness on my thighs,” noticing those improvements after only three days of regular use. That makes it a great anti-aging product for folks with dry or crepey skin .
 Michelle Rae Uy/CNN Underscored 
 To be clear, this isn’t a skin whitening product. Rather, Melasyl’s skin-brightening properties work incredibly well by managing excess melanin production and evening out your skin tone. I’ve been using this product for a few months now, and it’s been really effective on my tanned areas and sun spots. And I say this as someone who’s always out in the sun. The effects are more gradual, so you do have to be consistent with application.

 Bottom line
 Our testers agree that most of La Roche-Posay’s anti-aging products are effective, both as preventative care for younger skin and for targeting many mature skin concerns. They promote hydration, support elasticity and help protect the skin barrier without feeling too heavy or greasy. They are easy to dispense and apply, making them convenient for busy users and encourage healthy skin care habits. And the sunscreens, in particular, effectively protect our testers’ skin from UV radiation.
 FAQs
 Do dermatologists recommend La Roche-Posay?
 Although La Roche-Posay claims its products are “recommended by 100,000 dermatologists worldwide,” there’s no public proof of that. However, both Shah and Olamiju love the brand, with Shah saying she recommends some products to her patients and uses them herself. In addition, Olamiju said it’s “a great brand that’s been well vetted for a long time and very cutting edge.” If you peruse our other skin care coverage , you’ll find that La Roche-Posay is often recommended by other dermatologists too.
 Is La Roche-Posay considered high-end?
 In terms of quality and effectiveness, yes, La Roche-Posay’s products are high-quality. However, the cost of entry isn’t necessarily high. While they’re not in the budget range, the brand’s products are relatively affordable and accessible at many drugstores.
 What are the main skin concerns as people age?
 According to Shah, aging can show up in three ways: “When we think of aging, there are the fine lines and wrinkles, there are pigmentary issues, and then there’s volume loss.” The first two depend heavily on skin type and color. “People with lighter skin are usually going to initially notice more sunspots, hyperpigmentation and fine lines and wrinkles,” she said. Meanwhile, darker-skinned individuals “tend to age more with skin laxity so they may notice sagging more.”
 But there’s another important element to mature skin concerns. Olamiju said that “it’s important to remember that with these concerns, it’s cumulative.” Dynamic or expression lines, for example, can become static lines if you don’t address them early. “The earlier you address these problems, the easier [they are] to fix,” she said.
 What anti-aging products should everyone have in their daily routine?
 Both Shah and Olamiju stressed the importance of incorporating sunscreen in your daily routine as early as possible. “The base of any anti-aging regimen is sunscreen. It’s one of the best skin habits you can instill for skin protection and anti-aging. And it’s really never too early to start,” Shah said.
 When it comes to choosing a sunscreen, Olamiju said finding the right formulation that you will be encouraged to reapply throughout the day is key. The formulas we tested from La Roche-Posay are good contenders because of their lightweight feel and invisible finish.
 What should you look for when choosing anti-aging products?
 There’s really no straightforward answer to this. Some active ingredients work for some users; some work for others. So, it’s really all about a targeted, personalized, well-researched approach.
 That’s obviously easier said than done. With so many skin care products on the market, so many brands and so many new trending ingredients, choosing can feel overwhelming and intimidating for regular consumers.
 You can start by seeing a board-certified dermatologist for recommendations based on your specific skin type and needs. If seeing a dermatologist isn’t possible, both Shah and Olamiju highly recommend doing a lot of research, choosing well-established, science-backed ingredients, and sticking with established skin care companies that have “invested heavily in research and use ingredients with good data behind them.” La Roche-Posay stands out as one such brand, and hopefully this guide offers a good starting point.
